candidates.title: The forked honest PRT player (prt.lua 'honest' role without an epoch directory) and the vg.lua honest player keep only 8 input boundaries per epoch, so every per-match replay grows to about n/5 inputs
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua forked player: new_forked_player / new_forked_machine_cache), and the verification-game honest player doc/recipes/vg.lua (new_machine_cache)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support'); stands in for the honest operator as 'an implementation of an operator that no deployment runs' (section 3). vg.lua's player is in the same position (R1-R8-2 was rated on it the same way).

candidates.description: Same root cause as the confirmed R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1 (stored player, 32 boundaries), at two other sites that it does not cover. The forked PRT honest player, which prt.lua's own 'honest' role runs by default (no epoch directory), retains machines at input boundaries in a cache of DEFAULT_MACHINE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 8 entries. When the cache is full, consider() replaces an entry closer than input_gap to its predecessor, or doubles input_gap, so with n inputs the 8 retained boundaries end up about n/4 to n/8 apart. Every per-match unit (leaf proof, bundle opening during a bisection, uarch claim, uarch bundle) starts from new_machine_pair_at_epoch_input_offset, which forks the nearest retained entry and replays every input between it and the target (delivery plus a run to the fixed point, up to the per-input mcycle limit). The forked player has no agreed pair. Measured with the real module: the worst replay distance is 11 inputs at n=64, 191 at n=1024, 3071 at n=16384 and 12287 at n=65536, i.e. about n/5.3 (versus about n/16 for the stored player of R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1). At the PRT input limit of 2^24 inputs per epoch that is about 3.2 million full inputs per unit. vg.lua's honest player has the identical cache (capacity 8, gap 1) over epochs of up to 2^16 inputs; after the input-level bisection (which uses recorded per-input hashes) every dispute starts from reset_bisection and run_to_position forks the nearest retained entry, replaying up to about n/5 inputs (about 12k at 2^16) before it can answer within the disputed input, again in every dispute it plays. R12 bounds the cost of reaching the position of a per-match operation by 'the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds'; here it is bounded only by n/5 times the per-input usage.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender (section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts') fills an epoch with many inputs, then a dishonest claimant (any number of Sybils, section 7) steers each of the logarithmic number of matches it forces on the honest claim to a position just before a retained boundary (positions of the dispute are adversary-chosen: 'Steer the dispute to any position of the honest computation').
candidates.reachability: No emulator state is involved: any valid template and any application that accepts inputs reaches it once an epoch has more than 8 inputs. The cache policy is deterministic and the retained offsets are a function of n only (the experiment drives the real prt.lua cache code), so the adversary can compute the worst positions in advance.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: no exclusion fits. The trigger is input count and dispute positions, both adversary capabilities of section 7. 'Average-case performance that does not change the worst-case cost of any operation listed in R12' does not apply: the worst-case cost of reaching the position of a per-match operation grows with n. AUDIT.md excludes the validator nodes, dishonest strategies and test harnesses, not prt.lua's honest role or vg.lua. 2. Role: Support (AUDIT.md table). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator.' Both players are implementations of an operator that no deployment runs. 3. High/Medium cases: in the stood-in role the High constant-factor case ('multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor') does not fit, because the factor is n/5, which grows with the input count; so step 4 applies to the stood-in role, and the support Medium case ('A defect that only a support component shows, when section 3 rates it Medium') then fits. 4. Critical in the stood-in role: R12 'Each is measured from a machine at its starting position. Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary, which the application's per-input usage bounds. A7 must cover that cost a bounded number of times for every match'; section 8 Critical: 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make unbounded, super-linear, or larger than what the deployment was sized for' and 'violating any rule or obligation ... anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical'. So Medium for the support components. Alternative reading (same as R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1's): if 'nearest retained input boundary' lets an operator choose to retain few boundaries, it is Low. A further reading may treat vg.lua as a demonstration only (the R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1 fix note says its bounded cache may stay), which would make the vg.lua site Low or out of scope; the prt.lua forked honest player is the PRT recipe's default honest role and has no such excuse.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support standing in for a Critical R12 per-match cost); Low under the reading that excuses sparse retention; likely to be merged with R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1 by triage as a variant at another site
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness (section 1: the honest operator 'cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win'). An operator modelled on the forked player (or on vg.lua) spends about n/5 full inputs of replay per match unit; with clocks sized for the R12 per-input bound (A7), an input flood plus position steering makes it time out. The factor is about 3x worse than the confirmed stored-player case, and the forked player has no agreed-pair mitigation.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARGROWTH/cache-gap.lua, which requires the real doc/recipes/prt.lua module and drives prt.new_forked_machine_cache with fake machines (fork_server/set_cleanup_call/shutdown_server stubs), calling consider(i) for i = 1..n and computing the largest gap between retained boundaries: 'n=64 entries=8 worst replay=11 (n/5.8)', 'n=1024 worst=191 (n/5.4)', 'n=16384 worst=3071 (n/5.3)', 'n=65536 worst=12287 (n/5.3)'. vg.lua's consider() is line-for-line the same policy with the same constants (read, not run).
candidates.test_idea: Like bugs/R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1: build a tiny accept-everything rolling template (harness accept.bin), open prt.new_forked_player (or call the honest role's constructor) with geometry new_geometry(10), feed n = 512 inputs through event_handler.input_added, then wrap run_to_input_mcycle_offset (or machine:send_cmio_response through a counting proxy) and call event_handler.prove_state_transition / collect_mcycle_bundle at the input just before the 2nd retained entry (computed from player.machine_cache.entries). Assert that the number of inputs replayed is bounded by a constant independent of n (e.g. <= 2 for n = 512 and n = 2048); it fails on audit/prt2 (about n/5). Same for vg.lua: construct new_player with n inputs and count deliveries made by run_to_position after dispute_started.

not_covered: Enumerated and judged bounded or allowed, not reported (with reasoning): crisium listeners/remove_finished_epochs (bridges finish once settled irreversibly with no jobs; I looked for a job that could persist forever after settlement - eliminateMatchByTimeout needs !_isFinished but an alive match keeps the tournament unfinished, tryRecoveringBond pays an EOA signer once - and found none, so the 'retained epoch files grow with past epochs' path through an unfinished old bridge has no trigger I could find); prt-transactions journal (forget_settled drops settled nonces; candidates per nonce bounded by fee bumps to max_fee except the 'node dropped the candidate' re-sign path, not pursued); prt-log-history self.blocks and logs (bounded by the observed address set; growth only covered by R1-BOUNDARY-1/3 and R1-R12-3); bridge computations/prepared/rejected/invalid/reported/decoded caches (per match of the epoch); prt-epoch inputs/applied/history (inputs of open epochs, allowed by R12); prt-rpc (no caches); prt-websocket wait (drains queued headers, bounded per block); stored player epoch directory (inputs/, forests/ files never garbage-collected within an epoch but each tree stays referenced; per-input frontier_forest_store writes only non-durable trees; state.json lists uarch claims, O(matches) per match, negligible); stored machine cache (32 entries, R2-DFINPUTCOUNT-1); uarch claim forests (one hash per mcycle of the period, per match, allowed); emulator collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes reset_dirty_words (bounded by uarch state size), append_uarch_reset_root_hash (compressed pads).

Per-input cost of the stored player's commit (destroy, sync_stored, clone_stored of the whole machine to machine.revert, sync, load) is proportional to the machine size, not to what the input touched; R12 bounds per-input cost and storing/cloning linearly in bytes, so I judged it allowed and did not measure it (it matters on hosts without reflink, where many tiny inputs each copy the whole RAM image).

Restart cost: relaunch reopens the --keep-epochs finished epochs, whose listeners refetch every app InputAdded from the previous seal to the head and whose bridges refetch consensus and factory logs from their seal block; bounded by keep_epochs (operator option), so not reported beyond R1-BOUNDARY-1.

The PRT referee model (prt.lua referee, game-transport.lua) and vg.lua's referee were not enumerated under this angle; nor vg.lua's per-output proofs computed at seal (frontier_next_proofs over all outputs, about 2 KB per output), which I assume R1-R8-2 covers.

Emulator APIs: did not audit JSON-RPC server per-connection or fork bookkeeping (zombie/fork growth with age), page-hash-tree cache persistence, or dpt/dht growth; store/clone/sync costs on sparse images were not measured.
No chain experiment; the only run was the cache-gap experiment with the real prt.lua module and fake machines.
